elements.element: Customer owns every Deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 instead states that Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all other work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause does not grant Customer ownership of work product beyond Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor assigns its rights in Deliverables to Customer.
elements.evidence: There is no assignment; Vendor expressly retains exclusive ownership of Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor assigns its rights in other work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment of other work product appears.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of all pre-existing Vendor IP.
elements.evidence: Vendor retains Vendor Technology and owns generic tools and know-how, but the rendered language does not expressly cover all Vendor IP existing before the engagement.

elements.element: If Vendor IP is embedded in or required to use a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer a licence to that Vendor IP.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 provides that, to the extent Vendor Technology is incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable, the licence in Section 13.2 applies.

elements.element: The licence to embedded or required Vendor IP is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 expressly identifies the applicable Section 13.2 licence as perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to embedded or required Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The new language makes the licence to each Deliverable irrevocable, but Section 14.3 separately directs embedded or required Vendor Technology to Section 13.2, whose licence is not shown to be irrevocable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded or required Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The new language makes the Deliverable licence royalty-free, but the separate Section 13.2 licence governing embedded or required Vendor Technology is not shown to be royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Customer Data is not addressed.

elements.element: No joint ownership is created.
elements.evidence: The clause creates no joint ownership and instead provides for exclusive Vendor ownership of Deliverables and Vendor ownership or retention of its technology, tools, and know-how.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The added operative language expressly states, “Vendor owns its generic tools and know-how.”

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: The added operative language expressly states, “Vendor owns its generic tools and know-how.”

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to each Deliverable.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly refers to “Customer's licence to each Deliverable.”

elements.element: Customer's licence to each Deliverable is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly makes the licence perpetual and disapplies the Order Form term limitation.

elements.element: Customer's licence to each Deliverable is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly makes the licence irrevocable and disapplies the revocability limitation in Section 14.2.

elements.element: Customer's licence to each Deliverable is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly makes the licence worldwide.

elements.element: Customer's licence to each Deliverable is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly makes the licence royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use each Deliverable for its business.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits Customer to use each Deliverable for its business.

elements.element: Customer may modify each Deliverable for its business.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits Customer to modify each Deliverable for its business.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense each Deliverable for its business.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits Customer to sublicense each Deliverable for its business and disapplies Section 14.2's non-transferability limitation.

result.reason: The operative addition fully implements the fallback by confirming Vendor ownership of generic tools and know-how and granting Customer the required perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free rights to use, modify, and sublicense Deliverables for its business. It expressly disapplies the conflicting limitations in Section 14.2 without changing unrelated terms. The preferred position is not met because Vendor continues to own Deliverables, no assignment is provided, Customer Data is omitted, and the embedded Vendor Technology licence is not shown to be irrevocable or royalty-free.
